title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS — Strix Halo llama.cpp + native MTP
slug_note: First reported working native-MTP speculative decoding for the qwen4exp architecture on an AMD iGPU (ROCm), 16.8 -> 47.1 tok/s on a file rewrite.

variation.quant_detail: UD-IQ4_XS trunk + a separate Q8_0 MTP sidecar extracted with shard-scalpel (range reads, 5.2GB not 360GB)

engine.config: llama.cpp branch strix-halo-flash-next (ROCm). Three levers: GPU TOP_K fix (stock HIP falls back to CPU past ne=1024; PR #26592 hipCUB or #27466 native radix), native MTP (#27836) + detached-head loader fix, then ngram-mod: --spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod.

fork_revision.note: Two anchor-day commits; which one built the measured stack is unstated. Later commits 5ad68897a6a5/590ac45bc19b post-date the anchor and are excluded.

kernel_patches.note: Loader fix by crusaderky; whitelist rmonsurate/llama.cpp#1.

caveats: Output verified byte-clean at long prompts, but an earlier community MTP port produced plausible tok/s while emitting multilingual noise above ~1k prompt tokens — read the output, not just the counter.
Negative result (law 3): a commenter (2026-09-03) could not load the detached MTP sidecar on this branch under ROCm 10.0; the repro is broken on newer ROCm as of that date.
It is a custom llama.cpp branch with ROCm-specific fixes; it is not mainline and not stock ROCm.

known_failures.trigger: Detached Q8_0 MTP sidecar on the strix-halo-flash-next branch under ROCm 10.0 (gfx1151, Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 96 GB unified)

claims.statement: Serves the UD-IQ4_XS trunk plus the Q8_0 detached MTP sidecar on Strix Halo via the strix-halo-flash-next branch: GPU TOP_K fix, native MTP with loader fix, and --spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-mod.
Stock HIP falls back to CPU past ne=1024 for ggml_top_k; the branch fixes it via hipCUB (#26592) or native radix (#27466), worth +38-53% end-to-end at 24k.
claims.quote: stock HIP falls back to CPU past ne=1024 (no CUB)

claims.statement: Uses native MTP (#27836) with the detached-head loader fix; the Q8_0 head was extracted with HTTP range reads (5.2 GB fetched instead of the 360 GB checkpoint).
